report.title: Geometric GPU neighbor search: cell lists, stenciled cells and bounding-volume hierarchies

budget_assessment.judgment: Within the 1,300–1,700-word and seven-primary-URL limits. It compares the requested methods and build/query/reuse phases, gives measured examples and counterexamples with workload conditions, and separates measured claims from inferences.

scope_and_novelty_assessment.judgment: Finite and substantively answered, with no material scope overlap in the adjacent reviewed collections.
scope_and_novelty_assessment.scope_coverage: Covers direct all-pairs, uniform and stenciled cells, and linear or quantized BVHs; treats build, query/list emission, candidate work, storage, repeated force use, and Verlet rebuild correctness as separate costs. Direct all-pairs crossover is explicitly labeled as inference because the cited GPU papers do not measure it.
scope_and_novelty_assessment.overlap: R867 concerns GPU analytical-query fusion and materialization, R869 concerns GPU BFS frontier traversal, and R872 concerns relational equijoin methods. Their scope-review metadata establish adjacent exclusions; their held report bodies were not read for this review. R877's moving-particle geometry and distance-cutoff question is distinct.
scope_and_novelty_assessment.novel_increment: Introduces an independent geometric-search comparison with workload-specific evidence for cell/stencil and hierarchy crossovers, including candidate false positives, buffer reuse, and correctness limits. It does not imply adoption or transfer to Strata.
scope_and_novelty_assessment.conclusion: Archive as a useful held knowledge collection; no redundant follow-up scope is recommended.

depth_and_applicability.judgment: Coherent and adequately detailed for the requested comparison.
depth_and_applicability.strengths: Keeps the K80 and multi-GPU-generation paper results separate, distinguishes list-build gains from whole-run gains, includes hierarchy-loses and grid-favoring cases, and identifies candidate/output memory and periodic-image concerns. It gives explicit source-specific conditions and marks unmeasured direct-search and triclinic extrapolations as inference.
depth_and_applicability.limits: The evidence is historical CUDA/NVIDIA HOOMD-blue work; no SYCL, Intel Arc, Strata implementation, or target-device performance follows. The direct fused all-pairs crossover is conceptual only. The 2023 neighbor-list artifact study is GROMACS correctness evidence, not a GPU comparison.
depth_and_applicability.provenance_and_adoption: Research-only; no code, helper, test, product source, local measurement, or implementation adoption was proposed or inspected.

source_accuracy.status: The three cited primary studies and their titles were verified. The reviewed numerical and algorithmic details are consistent with the source papers, subject to the two source-context corrections below.
verified: Howard et al. 2016: K80/CUDA 7 single-precision setup; 192,000-particle periodic mixture; zero-buffer per-step rebuild; rBB and xB comparison; colloid/solvent parameters, rebuild counts, and build-versus-whole-run speedups; bin-width and memory-layout observations.

Howard et al. 2019: exact arXiv v2; HOOMD-blue 2.4.1 benchmark setup; cubic periodic systems; build-plus-traversal timing; K80, GTX 1080, P100 and V100 cases in single/double precision; 10-bit quantization, outward rounding, false-positive counts, and the sorted-grid versus atomic-grid limitation.

Kim, Fábián and Hummer 2023: DOI/title and author manuscript; missed interactions from an insufficient outer cutoff and infrequent GROMACS neighbor-list updates, pressure-tensor artifacts, membrane deformation under barostatting, water examples, and pressure oscillations associated with dynamic pruning.
source_accuracy.limits: The 2016 and 2019 values are paper-specific CUDA results with distinct timing boundaries; the 2023 paper does not compare GPU search performance. None establish an Arc/SYCL crossover. The review did not inspect local source or run experiments.

corrections.correction: The report identifies the 0.9× high-density single-precision result in the 2019 figure but omits the GPU. That specific ρ=0.8, N=128,000 result is Tesla K80; the same figure reports 1.0× on GTX 1080, 1.5× on P100, and 2.4× on V100. Preserve the K80 label when reusing this as the grid-favoring counterexample so the point is not generalized across devices.

The report says the WCA cutoff's low cell occupancy made grids less favorable. The 2019 source says BVH generally outperformed the grid by a larger factor for WCA, but specifically reports a smaller BVH speedup than for Lennard-Jones on the high-density GTX 1080 case: lower occupancy also meant fewer direct distance evaluations per particle for the grid. Preserve both effects and avoid treating low occupancy as a one-directional rule.

preserve_caveats: Historical NVIDIA CUDA and HOOMD-blue measurements do not establish SYCL or Arc behavior.
R877-C1: the 0.9× grid-favoring point is the high-density single-precision Tesla K80 case.
R877-C2: WCA's overall BVH advantage has a high-density GTX 1080 nuance; occupancy alone does not imply one crossover direction.
The 2019 sorted-grid baseline was roughly 2× slower than HOOMD-blue's optimized atomic grid in selected tests.
Direct fused all-pairs crossover is inference; cited papers did not measure it.
The 2023 GROMACS artifact study is correctness evidence, not a GPU benchmark.
